Title: Japan agrees to buy up to 8 mln barrels of Saudi crude to rebuild oil reserves
Article:
ISTANBUL: Japan has agreed to buy up to 8 million barrels of Saudi crude for its national petroleum reserve if market conditions are favourable, the two countries said Friday, Anadolu Ajansi reported, citing Saudi Press Agency.
The agreement also expands the storage capacity available to Saudi Arabia in Japan.
The kingdom, which already has access to 8 million barrels of capacity, will gain temporary use of storage for 16 million barrels, according to a joint statement carried by the Saudi Press Agency.
Saudi Arabia has already begun replenishing crude stocks at storage facilities in Japan, the statement said.
Saudi Energy Minister Prince Abdulaziz bin Salman and Japan's Economy, Trade and Industry Minister Ryosei Akazawa reached the agreement during a virtual meeting.
The ministers reaffirmed their commitment to cooperation on long-term energy security.
Japan is among the oil importers that drew on emergency reserves when the US-Iran war disrupted shipments through the Strait of Hormuz. Oil flows from Gulf producers have since recovered to near prewar levels, giving buyers an opportunity to rebuild depleted stockpiles.
For Saudi Arabia, storing crude in Japan puts supplies closer to Asian customers and makes them available if shipping through Hormuz is disrupted again.
Saudi Aramco Chief Executive Amin Nasser said last month that the kingdom had held talks with foreign governments about giving the state-owned oil company access to their strategic storage facilities.

Title: 'Every year my house floods': Rantau Panjang braces for rising waters
Article:
KOTA BARU: Residents in Rantau Panjang are keeping a close watch on Sungai Golok as its rising water level fuels fears of flooding, particularly if rain continues.
A Bernama survey found that intermittent rain and unpredictable weather had prompted residents to monitor the river closely, with heavy rainfall in nearby Narathiwat, Thailand, adding to their concerns.
Although the river has yet to overflow into residential areas, those living along its banks are taking precautions and preparing for possible flooding.
Resident Nik Ahmad Nik Ismail, 40, said the rising water level had prompted him to check the river more frequently.
"It is better to remain vigilant and keep abreast of the latest developments," he told Bernama today.
Another resident, Wan Che Zainab Wan Che Mat, 55, said heavy rain in Narathiwat had heightened anxiety among those living near the river.
Having experienced floods almost every year, she said she had become accustomed to her home being inundated but remained uneasy whenever the water level rose.
"My house is flooded almost every year. I am used to it, but I still feel worried whenever I see the river's water level rising," she said.
Yesterday, one of four river monitoring stations in Kelantan recorded a reading above the alert level as of 10.45pm.
Data from the Department of Irrigation and Drainage's Public Infobanjir portal showed that Sungai Golok at Rantau Panjang, Pasir Mas, had reached 7.18 metres, exceeding the alert level of 7 metres.

Title: ITMAX to raise RM1bil from sukuk issuances
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: ITMAX System Bhd has established two Islamic financing programmes with a combined limit of RM1 billion to fund its business operations and refinance existing borrowings.
The smart city solutions provider said its wholly owned ITMAX Capital Sdn Bhd lodged the required documents with the Securities Commission for an Islamic medium-term notes (IMTN) programme and an Islamic commercial papers (ICP) programme.
The IMTN has a perpetual limit, while the ICP has a tenure of up to seven years.
Individual issuances under the IMTN will have tenures of one year, while those under the ICP will range from one to 12 months.
ITMAX said the sukuk wakalah programmes are unsecured, although individual series or tranches may be issued on either an unsecured or secured basis.
Proceeds will be used for the group's Shariah-compliant general business, commodity purchases, refinancing of existing Shariah-compliant or conventional obligations, and future Shariah-compliant financing.
AmInvestment Bank Bhd is the principal adviser, lead arranger, lead manager, facility agent and security agent, while AmBank Islamic Bhd is the Islamic adviser.

Title: Three held as police uncover RM1.27mil stash of health and beauty products
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Police detained three men and seized health, cosmetic and food products worth RM1.27 million in a raid on a logistics premises in Banting, Selangor, yesterday.
The operation, codenamed Op Taring Dosej, was conducted at 12.10pm by the Bukit Aman Wildlife Crime Bureau/Special Intelligence Investigation, under the Internal Security and Public Order Department, with several enforcement agencies.
Bukit Aman Wildlife Crime Bureau/Special Intelligence Investigation commander Senior Assistant Commissioner Datuk Mohd Zaki Ashar said those detained were a local man believed to be the company owner and two Bangladeshi employees.
Checks uncovered 1,044 boxes of health and cosmetic products, 1,300 bottles of supplements and health products, 38 boxes of tremella soup products, 65 boxes of coenzyme Q10 products, as well as various tea-based food and beverage products and snacks.
"All seized items have been handed over to the respective enforcement agencies for further action and investigation under their respective jurisdictions," he said in a statement today.
The total value of the seizure was estimated at RM1.27 million, with the Health Ministry accounting for the bulk at RM1.26 million. The Kuala Langat District Health Office seized items worth RM5,167, while the Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Ministry accounted for RM4,745.
The operation also involved the Selangor Health Ministry's Pharmacy Division, the Customs Department's Klang branch, the Kuala Langat District Health Office, the Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Ministry and the Kuala Langat Municipal Council (MPKL).
The district health office issued two compounds totalling RM4,500, while MPKL issued another two amounting to RM2,000.
The case is being investigated under the Immigration Act 1959/63, Control of Drugs and Cosmetics Regulations 1984, Trade Descriptions Act 2011, Food Act 1983 and related regulations.
Zaki said police would continue to intensify enforcement and intelligence operations to curb smuggling and the distribution of illicit goods.

Title: Firefighters save woman threatening to jump into sea
Article:
LANGKAWI: Firefighters rescued a 35-year-old woman who threatened to jump into the sea from a breakwater at Kuala Muda here today.
Kedah Zone 4 Fire and Rescue Department chief Mohd Zamri Abdul Ghani said seven firefighters from the Padang Mat Sirat Fire and Rescue Station were dispatched to the scene after receiving an emergency call at 3.16pm.
"Upon arrival, firefighters found the woman on the breakwater, about 350 feet from the shoreline.
"She was believed to be experiencing emotional distress and had threatened to jump into the sea," he said.
Zamri said firefighters approached the woman and managed to persuade her to move to safety.
"She eventually agreed to leave the area and was escorted safely back to shore," he said.
The woman was unhurt and in stable condition before being handed over to the police.

Title: Evidence in former Petronas manager's case met international standards, court told
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Evidence stored by CyberSecurity Malaysia in the case involving former Petronas manager Mohd Khairul Akmal fully complied with international standards set by the American Society of Crime Laboratory Directors (ASCLD), the Sessions Court heard today.
CyberSecurity Malaysia Senior Digital Forensic Analyst Abdul Wafi Abdul Rahman, 38, said the agency's internal chain-of-custody procedures applied only within its forensic laboratory.
"The internal chain of custody applies only within the laboratory, involving the recipient, storekeeper and analyst. It does not include police investigating officers. These procedures apply only to internal processes after the exhibits have been handed over to us," he said.
The seventh prosecution witness was responding to questions during re-examination by Deputy Public Prosecutor Noor Syafina Mohd Radzuan in the trial of Mohd Khairul Akmal, who is charged with attempting to disclose Petronas' business report and financial structure to Petroleum Sarawak Bhd (Petros) on June 8, 2024.
Yesterday, Abdul Wafi told the court that he had examined a laptop belonging to the accused, two mobile phones and a USB drive between Dec 19, 2024 and Jan 24, 2025 to determine whether they contained any information related to the alleged attempt to transmit the documents.
Meanwhile, Abdul Wafi said he did not trace the location of Mohd Khairul Akmal's laptop, which was allegedly used in an attempt to send confidential information on the national oil company's business and financial structure to Petros, as this was the responsibility of telecommunications companies.
"It is not the responsibility of CyberSecurity Malaysia or myself to trace the location of the perpetrator or the whereabouts of the exhibits within the country, as that is the responsibility of telecommunications companies," he said.
He also said he did not analyse internet connection records in the laptop's event log when preparing the digital forensic report, as this was not within the scope of the investigation requested by the investigating officer.
"If the laptop had used an internet hotspot registered under another individual's name on the date of the incident, the connection activity should have been recorded in the log," he said.
Mohd Khairul Akmal, 41, is charged with attempting to disclose a document entitled 'Q1 2024 Upstream Business Performance Operational & Financial' to Petros, which he had obtained in the course of his duties as Petronas Business Unit Performance Manager, at a condominium unit in Jalan Pinang here, between 3.19 pm and 3.21 pm on June 8, 2024.
The charge is framed under Section 203A(1) of the Penal Code, read together with Section 511 of the same Code. Upon conviction, Section 203A(1) provides for a maximum fine of RM1 million or imprisonment for up to one year, while Section 511 provides for imprisonment of up to half the maximum term prescribed under Section 203A(1).
The trial before Judge Mazuliana Abdul Rashid continues on Feb 9 next year. – BERNAMA
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 'They were inseparable': Siblings, 13 and 10, die in house fire [WATCH]
Article:
TAWAU: "Muhammad Nor Fazryn always looked after his younger sister, wherever he went. They were inseparable. Sadly, neither made it out of the fire."
That was the heartbreaking account of their aunt, Noreen Malvine, 37, following the deaths of the siblings, aged 13 and 10, in a
house fire
at Taman Ria 11 here early today.
Noreen said her nephew, Muhammad Nor Fazryn Norman, and his 10-year-old sister, Nurailin Nathania, who was autistic, were trapped in an upstairs room of their double-storey terrace house when the fire broke out about 6am.
The room's windows were fitted with security grilles, leaving the children with no way out, she said.
Describing Nor Fazryn as an intelligent and protective older brother, Noreen said he was particularly attentive to Nurailin, whom he rarely left alone.
She said the children's mother, Nor Fazrina Edayu Faisal, had tried desperately to reach them but was eventually forced to escape through a second-floor bedroom window with her three other children when the roof collapsed.
"My sister-in-law fractured her spine when she jumped, while one of her children developed asthma after inhaling the thick smoke," she said.
Noreen said she took the injured mother and her three children to Tawau Hospital, while other family members continued searching for the two missing siblings.
The family later received confirmation that both children had been found dead.
She said Nor Fazrina Edayu was in stable condition but remained hospitalised for treatment. Her husband was making his way back to Tawau from his workplace in Kota Kinabalu.
Tawau Fire and Rescue Station chief Jemishin Ujin said the department received an emergency call at 6.13am and arrived at the scene nine minutes later.
"Upon arrival, we estimated that 70 per cent of the double-storey terrace house was already engulfed in flames.
"Firefighters used water from the fire engine's tank and a fire hydrant to put out the blaze before finding the two children dead in a room," he said.
The cause of the fire is still under investigation.

Title: MN Holdings lands record RM1.12bil solar deal
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: MN Holdings Bhd has secured its biggest contract to date, a RM1.12 billion deal as part of a consortium to build two large-scale solar farms in Kemaman, Terengganu.
The engineering and construction contract also marks the group's first entry into the large-scale solar segment.
MN Holdings will lead the consortium in delivering the two solar facilities, which have contracted export capacities of 250 megawatts alternating current (MWac) and 150MWac respectively, bringing their combined capacity to 400MWac.
The project was awarded by RE Kemaman Sdn Bhd and RE Kemaman II Sdn Bhd under the LSS Petra 5+ programme.
The scope covers the integrated design, engineering, procurement, construction, testing and commissioning of the facilities, including associated interconnection infrastructure and related works.
Work will begin upon receipt of the notice to proceed or limited notice to proceed from the clients, with completion targeted by 2028.
MN Holdings said it will pursue further opportunities in renewable energy projects, leveraging its existing technical capabilities and project execution experience.
Beyond its core engineering and construction business, the company is also exploring strategic equity investments in renewable energy projects.
"We believe this approach will support a more diversified earnings base and strengthen the company's long-term growth prospects," it said.

Title: Flood victims told to register or risk missing out on aid
Article:
KUALA SELANGOR: Flood victims have been advised to register with the authorities immediately, whether they are staying at temporary relief centres or in their own homes, to ensure they do not miss out on assistance.
Women, Family and Community Development Minister Datuk Seri Nancy Shukri said registration was crucial to ensure victims' details were recorded and aid could be distributed efficiently.
"We have channelled all the information, except for those who may have been left out due to timing and other factors.
"Whether they move to relief centres or remain at home, they still need to register so that we have their details on record. Those who register late may take a little longer to receive assistance," she said.
She was speaking after visiting flood victims at the relief centre at Sekolah Kebangsaan (SK) Dato' Maharaja Lela in Kampung Parit Omar, Jeram, today.
Also present were Selangor Social Welfare Department director Azmir Kassim and Kuala Selangor district officer Mohd Raiz Radzuan.
Nancy said the department was prepared for a possible increase in the number of evacuees should the flood situation worsen.
She said that 25 counsellors from the department and the Malaysian Board of Counsellors were on standby to provide psychosocial support to flood victims in Selangor.
A total of 1,817 victims from 503 families were reported to be staying at 14 relief centres across the state.
Nancy had previously told the Dewan Rakyat that flood victims who remained at home were also eligible to apply for the Bantuan Wang Ihsan compassionate aid, provided they registered with the authorities.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Sabah PH eyes more seats, but 3 remain non-negotiable
Article:
KOTA KINABALU: Sabah Pakatan Harapan (PH) will defend the three parliamentary seats it currently holds while exploring opportunities to contest additional seats in the 16th General Election (GE16).
Its chairman, Datuk Mustapha Sakmud, said the three seats were Sepanggar, which he represents, and Kota Kinabalu and Sandakan, currently held by DAP representatives.
He said Sabah PH's leadership had agreed to retain the seats as its baseline position during negotiations with other parties and coalitions ahead of the election.
"Our basic decision is to defend Sepanggar, Kota Kinabalu and Sandakan.
"We are also looking at the potential to contest other seats without jeopardising our cooperation with other partners," he told a press conference after a PH Sabah meeting here today.
Also present were Sabah Amanah chairman Datuk Lahirul Latigu, Sabah DAP deputy chairman Datuk Chan Foong Hin and Sabah PH secretary Datuk Ruji Ubi.
Mustapha declined to identify the additional seats Sabah PH was eyeing or disclose how many were under consideration.
He said formal negotiations with other political partners, particularly Gabungan Rakyat Sabah (GRS), had yet to begin.
"There have been no formal discussions with GRS so far, only informal engagements," he said.
On Sabah Barisan Nasional's (BN) proposal to establish a Muafakat Sabah pact with GRS, Mustapha said it was a view that the coalition was entitled to express.
At GE15 in November 2022, Sabah PH contested 24 parliamentary seats, with PKR fielding the most candidates at 10, followed by DAP with seven.
The coalition won three seats – Sepanggar, Kota Kinabalu and Sandakan.
Two other seats, Penampang and Tuaran, were also won under the PH banner but were represented by the United Progressive Kinabalu Organisation (Upko), which has since left the coalition.

Title: 'He kept his promise to care for mum until their final day'
Article:
BATU PAHAT: "My younger brother once promised us he would look after our mother. He kept that promise until their final day."
Those were the heartbreaking words of Abdul Hafiz Abd Muthaliff, 44, who lost his mother and younger brother after their rented house in
Kampung Parit Raja Darat
was gutted by fire early today.
His mother, Jamilah Bebe Abd Rahman, 63, and brother, Abdul Rahim Abdul Muthaliff, 36, were found burnt to death in their respective bedrooms.
Hafiz said he received the devastating news at 3.35am after being contacted by a relative at 2.45am.
"He called me and said, 'Hafiz, be strong. Your mother's house is on fire.'
"At first, he could not confirm whether anyone was inside. But when he later told me there were people in the house, I rushed here.
"I was so overwhelmed that I could no longer drive and had to ask another younger brother to help," he said when met at the forensic unit of Hospital Sultanah Nora Ismail (HSNI) here today.
Hafiz said he last spoke to his mother on Wednesday, when she called him twice, in the morning and again at night.
He said she had sounded particularly cheerful and even spoke of celebrating Hari Raya Aidilfitri together next year.
"She was so happy that day. She even said she wanted to celebrate Hari Raya with me next year. I never imagined that would be among our last conversations.
"Last night, my brother also sent a TikTok message to my youngest child, asking what the child was doing and enquiring about me and my wife. He also asked when we would be coming over.
"We had no idea it would be his final message," he said.
Meanwhile, Jamilah Bebe's daughter, Jabeera, 40, said losing her mother and younger brother in the same tragedy was particularly devastating, especially as the family had lost an aunt just a week earlier.
"All this while, we only read news about such tragedies happening to other families. This time, it has happened to our own.
"I accept what has happened. May Allah place them both in paradise," she said.
In a statement, Batu Pahat district police chief Assistant Commissioner Shahrulanuar Mushaddat Abdullah Sani said the deaths of the two victims had been classified as sudden deaths.
He said the fire was believed to have broken out while both victims were asleep in their respective bedrooms.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Moody's affirms Affin's A3 rating
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Moody's Ratings has reaffirmed Affin Group's long-term credit rating at A3 with a stable outlook, citing its sound financial fundamentals, good asset quality and support from Sarawak.
Moody's said Affin's rating reflected its standalone creditworthiness, as captured by its baa2 baseline credit assessment, alongside support from its major shareholder, the Sarawak state government.
"Moody's expects Affin Group to maintain healthy asset quality, with its tangible common equity to risk-weighted assets ratio remaining in the 14 per cent to 15 per cent range in 2027.
"Its funding and liquidity positions are also expected to remain healthy, supported by efforts to grow current and savings account deposits," it said in a statement.
Affin Group president and group chief executive officer Datuk Wan Razly Abdullah said the reaffirmation reflected confidence in the group's long-term growth prospects.
"This recognition elevates our credit standing on the global stage and enhances our access to funding and capital markets worldwide as we continue to execute Affin Axelerate 2028 Strategic Plan," he said.
For the first nine months of 2026, the group recorded a 41.5 per cent increase in operating profit to RM720 million from RM509 million a year earlier.
Gross loans and financing grew 14 per cent to RM86.7 billion, while customer deposits rose 5.4 per cent to RM82.4 billion.
Total assets increased 11.5 per cent year-on-year to RM132 billion as at September 2026.

Title: Negri MB shuts door on bid to remove Tuanku Muhriz
Article:
SEREMBAN: Negri Sembilan Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim has declared the April 19 proclamation seeking to remove Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir as the state's ruler invalid, saying it will not be gazetted.
He also reaffirmed his allegiance to Tuanku Muhriz, declaring that the state government would neither recognise another individual as Yang di-Pertuan Besar nor support any attempt to challenge the ruler's position.
"The state government will not recognise anyone else as Yang di-Pertuan Besar or revive the April 19 proclamation or any related documents.
"I reaffirm that Tuanku Muhriz remains the legitimate Yang di-Pertuan Besar of Negri Sembilan," he told a press conference at the Menteri Besar's official residence here today.
The
proclamation
, issued amid a dispute involving the state's traditional ruling chiefs, or Undang, sought to depose Tuanku Muhriz and replace him with Tuanku Nadzaruddin Tuanku Ja'afar.
The
Attorney-General's Chambers
had previously declared the move unconstitutional, while the Dewan Keadilan dan Undang (DKU), the state's royal and customary council, maintained that Tuanku Muhriz remained the legitimate ruler.
Ismail made the declaration after an audience with Tuanku Muhriz at Istana Hinggap this morning. He was appointed Menteri Besar on Aug 2.
Also present at the palace were Undang Luak Rembau Datuk Hassan Ab Hamid, Undang Luak Sungai Ujong Datuk Muhammad Faris Johari and Undang Luak Jelebu Datuk Azrin Khairi.
Ismail said he would uphold the State Constitution and recognise the powers vested in the DKU.
"With the Quran as my witness, I swear to respect and pledge my loyalty to the Yang di-Pertuan Besar of Negri Sembilan and the royal institution, uphold and safeguard the sovereignty of the State Constitution, and recognise the powers vested in the Dewan Keadilan dan Undang," he said.
He also pledged not to allow any state assemblyman, government department, agency or official to take action that could undermine the ruler's sovereignty, position, powers, rights or privileges.
Ismail acknowledged that Datuk Mubarak Dohak and Datuk Maarof Mat Rashad had ceased to hold the positions of Undang Luak Sungai Ujong and Undang Luak Jelebu, respectively, in accordance with their customary laws.
He said Datuk Abdul Rahim Yasin had never been validly appointed Undang Luak Rembau as the required customary installation ceremony had not been completed.
"These three individuals therefore have no legal authority to exercise any powers under Article 10 of the Negri Sembilan State Constitution 1959," he said.
Ismail said matters concerning the appointment, succession or removal of traditional ruling chiefs would be referred to the DKU under Article 16(2) of the State Constitution, where necessary.
He also pledged to recognise and implement all decisions made by the council, including having them gazetted promptly where required.
"I undertake, without reservation, to recognise and implement all decisions of the Dewan, whether already made or to be made," he said.
The state government would also withdraw official recognition, allowances, residences, staff and other privileges from individuals whom the DKU had determined no longer held the office of Undang.
Those recognised by the council, meanwhile, would receive the facilities and privileges attached to their positions without delay.
"These facilities, recognition and privileges will be provided immediately," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Wawasan Dengkil's Q1 profit slips 23pct
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Wawasan Dengkil Holdings Bhd's net profit fell 23.33 per cent to RM2.07 million in the first quarter (Q1) ended September 30, 2026 compared to RM2.70 million a year earlier due to higher administrative expenses.
In its filing with Bursa Malaysia, the company said its revenue rose 11.28 per cent to RM59.18 million in Q1 2026 compared to RM53.18 million last year.
"The revenue for the quarter was mainly contributed by the construction services segment, which accounted for 98.70 per cent of total revenue, with the main contributions from UMW Precinct 5C p
roject.
"This was followed by contributions from Central Spine Road and Sungai Long Project," it said.
Barring any unforeseen circumstances, Wawasan Dengkil said it remains cautiously optimistic of its prospects for the coming financial year.
"Supported by our sizeable order book, our alignment with national infrastructure and energy transition priorities, a broader market presence and an emerging platform in renewable energy generation, we are well positioned to pursue growth opportunities," it added.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 'No time, I'm in a rush': Jalaluddin sidesteps MB controversy
Article:
JELEBU: Negri Sembilan Umno liaison committee chairman Datuk Seri Jalaluddin Alias today declined to comment on the Menteri Besar controversy, saying he was in a hurry.
"Sorry, I don't have time for a press conference. I'm in a rush," he told reporters before leaving a housing project groundbreaking ceremony in Simpang Pertang after receiving a phone call.
Earlier, Jalaluddin, who is also Pertang assemblyman, had jokingly warned reporters against asking him about Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim.
"There will be no press conference on that matter. Just ask about the housing project. I don't want to comment on the Menteri Besar," he said.
Sources said Jalaluddin had declined to comment as any official statement on the issue should come from Umno president Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi.
Earlier today, Ismail, 67, who is also Juasseh assemblyman, announced that he would
remain as Negri Sembilan Menteri Besar
.
He made the announcement at a press conference at the Menteri Besar's official residence following an audience with the Yang di-Pertuan Besar of Negri Sembilan Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir at Istana Hinggap this morning.

Title: YTL Power denies links to Nvidia GPU allegations
Article:
Azanis Shahila Aman
KUALA LUMPUR: YTL Power International Bhd today denied allegations linking its Johor data centres to the alleged transfer of Nvidia graphics processing units (GPUs) to Chinese customers.
The group described the reports as speculative and untrue.
YTL Power said its data centre subsidiary YTL Data Centers provides co-location services including space, power, cooling and connectivity to multiple global customers, including US hyperscalers.
It stressed that these arrangements comply with Malaysian laws and US trade controls.
The group added that it has worked closely with the Investment, Trade and Industry Ministry on its data centre developments and met all applicable reporting and import requirements.
The denial comes amid heightened scrutiny over the use of US-made advanced semiconductors, particularly Nvidia GPUs, in overseas data centres and concerns that computing capacity located in third countries could be accessed remotely by Chinese companies.
The US Commerce Department's Bureau of Industry and Security issued an interim final rule on Nov 19 to prevent companies in countries of concern, including China, from accessing large volumes of advanced computing power through data centres overseas.
The new rules impose licensing requirements on certain advanced semiconductor exports to Malaysia, Indonesia, Singapore, Thailand and Brazil.
They also target overseas data centres that provide significant computing capacity to companies headquartered in China or other restricted destinations.
YTL Power said the new rules do not affect its co-location services, as the provisions cited by the group focus on semiconductor importers and providers of computing services to customers in restricted destinations.
It expressed confidence that demand for co-location data centre infrastructure in Malaysia will continue to expand, supported by strong global demand, including from US customers.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Selangor bears brunt as 2,372 flood victims remain displaced
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A total of 2,372 flood victims from 685 families remain at 24 temporary relief centres (PPS) in four states as of 4.30pm today.
According to the Social Welfare Department's Info Bencana portal, the affected states are Selangor, Perak, Negri Sembilan and Sarawak.
Selangor continued to record the highest number of evacuees, with 1,786 victims from 489 families housed at 14 centres across four districts.
Kuala Selangor accounted for the bulk of the evacuees, particularly in the Ijok and Jeram subdistricts.
Among the centres, Sekolah Kebangsaan (SK) Dato' Maharaja Lela was sheltering 394 victims, followed by SK Parit Mahang (365) and Sekolah Rendah Agama Bukit Kuching (236).
Other centres in the district included Dewan Orang Ramai Bukit Kuching Tengah (139 victims), SK Rantau Panjang (134), Sekolah Agama Batu 8 Ijok (120), SK Jaya Setia (97), KAFA Integrasi Hidayah Bukit Cherakah (66), Dewan Orang Ramai Seri Harmoni (62) and SK Sultan Abdul Aziz (nine).
Elsewhere in Selangor, two centres remained open in Klang – SK Sungai Binjai in Meru, sheltering 113 victims, and Dewan Masjid An-Naim Kampung Jalan Kebun in Seri Andalas.
[[nid:1582090]]
SK Batu Arang in Rawang was the sole centre operating in Gombak, housing 25 victims, while Balai Raya Kampung Sungai Kelambu in Tanjung Sepat, Kuala Langat, sheltered another 20.
In Perak, 477 victims from 163 families were housed at seven centres across five districts.
Kerian recorded the highest number of evacuees, with 144 victims from 46 families at SK Parit Haji Aman and SK Bukit Merah in Bagan Serai.
Manjung had 131 victims from 39 families at SRA Rakyat Padang Serai, while Hilir Perak recorded 97 victims from 31 families at Dewan Rumah Rehat MPTI Bandar Baru.
In Perak Tengah, 90 victims from 41 families were sheltering at SK Tanjong Belanja and SK Dato' Sagor.
Another 15 victims from six families were housed at SK Batu Hampar along Jalan Taiping-Beruas in Larut, Matang and Selama.
In Negri Sembilan, 50 victims from 14 families remained at SK Jimah in Lukut, Port Dickson.
Sarawak also recorded 50 evacuees from 16 families, with two relief centres still operating across two districts.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Seven RMAF personnel held over RM4.83mil drug haul
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Seven Royal Malaysian Air Force (RMAF) personnel, including five officers, have been detained to assist investigations into the discovery of 96.6kg of suspected drugs at Subang Air Base on Tuesday.
RMAF chief General Tan Sri Muhamad Norazlan Aris said the other two detainees were personnel of different ranks.
He said the air force would not tolerate any misconduct or involvement by its personnel in drug smuggling and trafficking, particularly activities involving military aircraft and assets, regardless of rank or position.
"The RMAF took immediate action following the discovery, including detaining individuals suspected of being involved, notifying the police and handing them over to the police Narcotics Criminal Investigation Department (NCID) for further investigation.
"The RMAF will continue to provide full cooperation to the police to ensure a comprehensive investigation is conducted and appropriate action is taken against any parties found guilty," he said in a statement.
The discovery
was made by RMAF personnel at the Air Movement Section (AMS) building at Subang Air Base.
Norazlan said initial inspections found that the suspicious luggage did not bear security screening stickers to indicate that it had undergone the required checks.
"Further inspections by personnel from the RMAF Ground Defence Force (Handau), using scanning machines, detected several suspicious packages neatly arranged inside the luggage," he said.
Earlier today,
two RMAF personnel were remanded
for seven days to assist police investigations into a drug trafficking operation allegedly involving military aircraft.
The suspects, a 28-year-old corporal and a 48-year-old warrant officer 2, were brought before magistrate Don Stiwin Malanjum at the magistrate's court here. They had been arrested during a police operation early today.
Their arrests are believed to be linked to the trafficking of 96.64kg of methamphetamine, worth RM4.83 million, involving
five RMAF officers
and six civilians.
Norazlan said the RMAF's swift response, including detecting the incident, making initial arrests and handing the suspects over to the authorities, reflected its commitment to preventing such activities.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Aeon's Q3 earnings fall 36pct on higher tax expenses
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Aeon Co (M) Bhd's net profit fell 36.30 per cent to RM9.30 million in the third quarter ended Sept 30, 2026, from RM14.60 million a year ago, dragged by a sharp increase in tax expenses despite improved operating performance.
Bursa Malaysia filing showed the retailer's tax expense surged to RM17.30 million from RM4 million, mainly due to higher deferred tax charges, which rose to RM16.70 million from RM1 million.
Aeon said its effective tax rate was higher than the statutory rate mainly due to expenses that were not deductible for tax purposes.
Quarterly revenue rose 1.59 per cent to RM1.01 billion from RM995.20 million, supported by higher contributions from its retail and property management businesses.
Retail revenue increased 1.03 per cent to RM811 million from RM802.70 million, as consumer spending remained focused on essential purchases while discretionary spending stayed subdued.
Revenue from property management services grew 3.90 per cent to RM200 million from RM192.50 million, driven by sustained occupancy rates and successful tenancy renewals.
Despite the decline in net profit, Aeon's operating profit rose 18.12 per cent to RM50.20 million from RM42.50 million, supported by effective cost management and improved operational efficiency.
For the first nine months, Aeon's net profit rose 12.84 per cent to RM107.20 million from RM95 million a year ago, while revenue edged up 0.28 per cent to RM3.25 billion from RM3.24 billion.
The stronger nine-month earnings were mainly driven by higher contributions from property management services and disciplined cost management.
On prospects, the company expects the opening of Aeon Mall KL Midtown in the final quarter to expand its property management portfolio and support growth.
It also plans to capitalise on the upcoming festive shopping season through targeted promotions and customer engagement initiatives.
Aeon said it would continue expanding its private-label offerings, enhancing its loyalty programme and investing in digital transformation and asset improvements.
The company remains cautious about the global economic outlook and its potential impact on consumer sentiment and spending patterns.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: SFP Tech's Q3 earnings surge eightfold to RM5.81mil on stronger manufacturing demand
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: SFP Tech Holdings Bhd's net profit surged more than eightfold to RM5.81 million in the third quarter ended Sept 30, 2026, from RM699,000 a year ago, as revenue more than doubled to RM48.50 million from RM21.65 million.
In a filing with Bursa Malaysia, the company attributed the stronger performance mainly to increased manufacturing activities and higher customer orders.
The manufacturing segment remained the main revenue contributor, generating RM40.86 million, up 118.78 per cent from RM18.68 million a year ago. It accounted for 84.26 per cent of the group's quarterly revenue.
The automation segment contributed the remaining RM7.63 million, compared with RM2.97 million previously.
Malaysia and the United States remained the group's largest markets, contributing a combined RM34.32 million, or 70.76 per cent of quarterly revenue.
For the first nine months, SFP Tech's net profit rose 82.76 per cent to RM15.21 million from RM8.32 million a year ago, while revenue increased 60.46 per cent to RM113.89 million from RM70.98 million.
As at Sept 30, the group had cash and bank balances, including deposits, of RM16.41 million, compared with RM9.68 million at end-December 2025.
Total liabilities increased to RM129.71 million from RM104.74 million, while borrowings rose to RM67.17 million from RM56.44 million.
Looking ahead, SFP Tech said its business outlook remained positive, supported by customer diversification and expansion into new markets.
The group secured six major customers across the medical, defence, energy and mining sectors during the first nine months of 2026.
New customers in Australia had also begun contributing to revenue, supporting its expansion into the Australian and New Zealand markets.
SFP Tech's order book stood at RM143.80 million as at Oct 30, with its book-to-bill ratio remaining above 1.2 times for three consecutive quarters.
The group said it would continue to pursue new customers and expand its presence across key industries and markets while remaining mindful of geopolitical uncertainties and changing global market conditions.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Bangladesh hit by fresh arson attacks amid political unrest
Article:
DHAKA: Fresh arson attacks erupted in Bangladesh on Friday as authorities restored communications with the hometown of convicted former prime minister Sheikh Hasina, following days of unrest over her planned return from exile.
Hasina, 79, has vowed to return to Bangladesh in December from India, despite being sentenced to death in absentia for crimes against humanity over a deadly crackdown during the 2024 uprising that ousted her.
Hasina's former ruling party, the Awami League, whose activities are now banned, called for strikes this week to mark the anniversary of the day she received her death sentence.
Hundreds of paramilitary troops have been deployed to contain the unrest, in which at least three people have been killed.
A petrol bomb was hurled at the residence of a junior foreign minister, Humaiun Kobir, in the northeastern city of Sylhet on Friday, police said.
Kobir said Dhaka would deal with attacks "very firmly".
"It is not possible to bring back a 'fled terrorist' by throwing petrol bombs," he told reporters on Friday.
Hasina has repeatedly said she wants to return next month, telling AFP in an email this week that she was "fully aware" she could be hanged.
Attackers also set fire to the home of a former junior foreign minister from the Awami League in Rajshahi on Thursday.
[[nid:1582076]]
Protesters wielding machetes also torched a police station in Gopalganj, Hasina's political stronghold, on the same day. Communications have since been restored.
Police said 124 people linked to the Awami League had been arrested in the capital, Dhaka, over the past 24 hours, without providing further details.
The family home of Nobel laureate and former interim leader Muhammad Yunus in the port city of Chittagong was also targeted in an arson attack.
Grameen Bank, founded by Yunus, said more than 20 of its branches had been targeted in arson attacks this month.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: RHB banks secure top AAA rating
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: RAM Ratings has upgraded the financial institution ratings of RHB Bank Bhd, RHB Islamic Bank Bhd and RHB Investment Bank Bhd to AAA/Stable/P1 from AA1/Positive/P1.
RHB today said the upgrade was underpinned by the group's strengthened funding profile, strong capitalisation, healthy asset quality and sustained profitability.
Group managing director and group chief executive officer Datuk Mohd Rashid Mohamad said the AAA rating reflected years of disciplined execution, prudent risk management and continued confidence from customers, shareholders and business partners.
He said the recognition also reflected the group's efforts to strengthen its businesses, improve its customer value propositions and deliver sustainable financial performance.
"An AAA rating is not achieved overnight. It reflects years of disciplined execution, prudent risk management and, above all, the trust that our customers, shareholders and partners continue to place in RHB," he said.
Rashid said the milestone would reinforce the group's resolve to serve customers better and support the growth of the communities and markets in which it operates.
The upgrade also marks progress under the group's PROGRESS27 strategy, which focuses on strengthening its businesses and creating sustainable long-term value for stakeholders.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Betel-leaf stall, two sundry shops sealed in Penang crackdown on foreign-run businesses
Article:
GEORGE TOWN: Three businesses operating without valid licences were sealed by the Penang Island City Council (MBPP) during an enforcement operation targeting foreign-run premises and licensing violations.
The council conducted Ops Tegas from 4.30pm yesterday, deploying 21 officers from its Licensing, Enforcement and Corporate Communications and Public Relations departments.
The operation covered three locations — Jalan Oldham in Tanjung Bungah, Jalan Sungai and Jalan Tun Dr Awang in Bukit Jambul — focusing on unlicensed trading and businesses operated by foreigners.
At a premises in Jalan Oldham, officers found an unlicensed business selling betel leaves (sirih) and beverages without a valid 2026 council permit.
"Three foreigners were found at the premises, including one without valid identification documents.
"Enforcement officers ordered all three to leave before disposing of the raw ingredients and drinks," the council said in a Facebook post.
Over at Jalan Sungai, a sundry shop was caught operating without a 2026 licence, with a foreign worker manning the premises.
The operator claimed a composite licence application was in the midst of being submitted.
Another sundry shop along Jalan Tun Dr Awang in Bukit Jambul was also found operating without a valid 2026 permit. Officers removed and seized its business banner.
Following the inspections, MBPP sealed all three premises under the Local Government Act 1976.
The council also issued notices prohibiting the operators from tampering with the seizure tape, re-entering the premises to conduct business or resuming operations until the issues identified were resolved.
MBPP said Ops Tegas would continue to target unlicensed traders, non-compliant foreign-operated businesses and commercial activities that disrupted public order across the island.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 32 transactions, RM85,468 missing: NGO director arrested
Article:
KANGAR: An NGO director has been arrested at Kuala Lumpur International Airport Terminal 2 (KLIA2) over the alleged misappropriation of RM85,468 in organisational funds.
Perlis police chief Deputy Commissioner Hamzah Hashim said the 31-year-old man was detained at the domestic arrival gate at 11.05am today after arriving on a flight from Sabah.
He said the arrest followed intelligence gathering and was linked to a criminal breach of trust investigation opened on Nov 13.
"Investigations revealed that the alleged misappropriation of funds belonging to the organisation, which is based in Jalan Behor here, took place between March 2 and July 20 this year.
"The case involved 32 transactions in which funds were transferred into the suspect's personal bank account," he said in a statement today.
Hamzah said the suspect was expected to be remanded tomorrow to assist investigations under Section 409 of the Penal Code for criminal breach of trust.
The offence carries a jail term of between two and 20 years, whipping and a fine upon conviction.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Parking row sparks Cheras brawl; two Chinese citizens arrested after violent clash
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A dispute over a parking space erupted into a violent brawl involving several men armed with suspected iron rods outside a convenience store in Taman Connaught, Cheras, early today.
Two Chinese citizens, aged in their late 20s and early 30s, were arrested following the incident outside a MyNews outlet near Maxim D'Perc Residence around 4am.
Cheras police chief Assistant Commissioner Mohd Rosdi Daud said police received a report on the fight, which was believed to have stemmed from a misunderstanding over vehicle parking.
"Acting on information received, personnel from the Cheras police headquarters' D7 Division arrested two Chinese citizens at Jalan 9, Taman Len Seng, at 5am.
"Both men sustained injuries to their heads and faces and were taken for medical treatment," he said in a statement today.
Rosdi said preliminary examination of closed-circuit television (CCTV) footage revealed that several other people were also involved in the altercation.
"Initial investigations indicate that the weapons used during the fight were iron rods," he said.
He said both suspects were brought before a magistrate and remanded for four days, from today until Nov 23, to facilitate investigations.
The case is being investigated under Section 148 of the Penal Code for rioting while armed with weapons.
Videos of the brawl have since gone viral on social media.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: [UPDATED] RMAF drug trafficking probe: 2 more arrested in Tawau, bringing total to 7
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Two more Royal Malaysian Air Force (RMAF) personnel have been arrested in Tawau, Sabah, bringing the number of air force personnel held in connection with a cross-border drug trafficking syndicate to seven.
The latest arrests bring the total number of suspects detained to 13, including six civilians, among them two alleged syndicate coordinators, following operations in the Klang Valley, Labuan and Sabah.
Bukit Aman Narcotics Crime Investigation Department (NCID) director Datuk Hussein Omar Khan confirmed that the two RMAF personnel, a 28-year-old corporal and a 48-year-old warrant officer II, were arrested at the air force base in Tawau and remanded to assist investigations.
"The two who were remanded are the latest arrests made at RMAF Tawau.
"The total number of RMAF personnel arrested now stands at seven," he said when contacted today.
The arrests come as police widen their investigation into
a syndicate
suspected of exploiting military aviation facilities to transport drugs from Peninsular Malaysia to Sabah.
The operation followed an NCID investigation that led to the seizure of 96.64kg of methamphetamine worth RM4.83 million.
Investigators believe the syndicate used access to military aviation facilities to move narcotics across the South China Sea, with Sabah serving as a transit point before the drugs were smuggled to neighbouring countries, including Indonesia and the Philippines.
Police are also tracing the alleged mastermind behind the operation.
The case has raised concerns over the use of military aviation facilities by organised drug trafficking syndicates seeking to bypass conventional airport security and enforcement checks.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Bank Negara, Philippines' Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas deepen ties in Islamic finance, digital payments
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Bank Negara Malaysia and the Philippines' Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas (BSP) have signed a memorandum of understanding (MoU) to strengthen cooperation in several key areas.
Bank Negara governor Datuk Seri Abdul Rasheed Ghaffour said these include Islamic finance, cross-border payment linkages, local currency transactions, financial innovation and digitalisation.
He said the MoU comes at an opportune time as the financial and economic landscape grows increasingly complex.
"Building on our strong partnership, it enables Bank Negara and BSP to advance shared priorities, learn from each other, pursue new opportunities and navigate emerging challenges together," he said in a statement.
BSP governor Eli M Remolona Jr said the MoU marked another important step in the longstanding partnership between the two central banks.
"We have built a strong foundation, and now the real test is turning it into stronger institutions, better financial infrastructure and practical programmes that genuinely improve life for our people," he said.
Both central banks said they looked forward to translating the framework into meaningful cooperation that would deliver tangible benefits for their economies and promote deeper regional financial integration.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 'Bonebridge' implant opens up new world of hearing for Amirul
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A 19-year-old student born without external ears and with congenital hearing loss is experiencing a new lease of life after undergoing a Bonebridge hearing implant procedure at the Canselor Tuanku Muhriz Hospital (HCTM) on Nov 12.
The implant, which is placed beneath the skin behind the ear, uses bone conduction to transmit sound vibrations through the skull directly to the inner ear, bypassing parts of the outer and middle ear.
Unlike conventional hearing aids, which amplify sound through the ear canal, the Bonebridge system consists of an internal implant and an external audio processor worn over the implant site.
For Muhammad Amirul Hakimi Sani, who previously relied on conventional hearing aids, the procedure has improved his ability to hear, boosting his confidence in socialising and keeping up with his studies.
The Form Six student of SMK Munshi Abdullah in Batu Berendam, Melaka, said he had been ridiculed by some people who did not understand his condition.
"I have been called 'earless', and some people have even asked angrily whether I was deaf when I could not hear what they were saying. They did not know that I had been hearing-impaired since birth.
"It was upsetting because I did not ask to be born with this condition, but I am still happy being myself. I believe Allah gave me this uniqueness so that I would not hear things that are bad or of no benefit.
"Previously, people had to speak loudly and stand close to me, often repeating themselves to make sure I understood. With the implant, I can now hear much better," he said when contacted today.
The eldest of three siblings said he had never regretted his condition, choosing instead to regard it as a blessing that had taught him to become a better person and remain grateful.
However, he admitted that being mocked had made him feel sad and less confident about mixing with his peers.
Amirul Hakimi attended special education classes under the Integrated Special Education Programme (PPKI) throughout primary and secondary school until Form Five, relying on sign language before continuing to Form Six.
He said the transition to Form Six had been challenging because his teachers did not use sign language, making it difficult for him to follow lessons due to his limited hearing.
"Previously, I used conventional hearing aids that could be removed for daily activities and studying. However, whenever I sweated, I had to take them off.
"Following lessons in Form Six was difficult because of my limited hearing and the fact that my teachers did not use sign language. But I felt a new sense of hope when the doctor told me about this implant.
"I never expected to be part of this surgery performed by the HCTM medical team. I was initially afraid, but I put my faith in Allah and the doctors' expertise. I am glad the first surgery was successful," he said.
Muhammad Amirul Hakimi expressed gratitude for the support of his parents, Sani Muin, 51, and Noorkamariah Tahir, 45, as well as the HCTM medical team and everyone who helped cover the cost of the surgery.
He said the experience had also renewed his determination to pursue his studies and fulfil his ambition of becoming a special education teacher.
"I will make the most of this device. It has also motivated me to study harder and achieve my dream of becoming a special education teacher.
"I want to prove that I can succeed too, and that our limitations should never stand in the way of achieving our goals," he said.
Meanwhile, his mother, Noorkamariah, said Amirul had initially been reluctant to undergo the implant surgery because he did not want to burden the family financially, as he was not working and his father was a lorry driver.
"I also hope the implant will help him with his studies and give him greater confidence when interacting with others," she said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Taking the ECRL? Here’s what to expect onboard, including one very Malaysian necessity (VIDEO)
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 20 — The excitement of taking a new train service is really about the experience and discovering what amenities await.

As the East Coast Rail Link (ECRL) prepares to connect communities across the east coast when commercial passenger services begin next month, here’s what passengers can expect from the onboard six-car electric train experience.

One of the first things passengers may notice is the generous legroom. The surprise is it serves a purpose beyond passenger comfort.

It actually allows the seats to swivel and face each other, giving families and groups travelling together greater flexibility in their seating arrangements.

Beyond the swivel seating arrangement, passengers can also choose between two travel classes: Economy and Business, each offering its own level of comfort and amenities.

All seats feature patterned blue upholstery and fold-down tray tables that can support up to 25kg, with Business Class arranged in a 2-2 configuration and Economy Class in a 3-2 layout.

The main difference? The Business Class seats come with headrests, a plusher, more cushioned feel and a wider seat base for added comfort.

An onboard bistro in the middle section of the train also allows passengers to purchase pre-heated meals, refreshments and beverages, with train crew available around the clock to serve them.
In addition, passengers travelling in Business Class receive full meal service served by crew members trained at the Malaysia Airlines Academy, bringing airline-style dining service to the rail journey.

Despite travelling at speeds of up to 160km/h, passengers can also expect a relatively quiet ride, with minimal noise from outside the train.

Other amenities include a dedicated prayer room, hot and cold water dispensers, a diaper-changing area and wheelchair-accessible facilities throughout the train.

For added convenience, passengers can also enjoy WiFi connectivity, and digital displays provide real-time information on the train’s speed, temperature and upcoming destinations.

And for those concerned about the cabin temperature, the train’s climate control system maintains an indoor temperature between 19°C and 21°C to keep passengers comfortable throughout the journey.

And last but not least, yes, every washroom includes a bidet, a familiar convenience that many Malaysian passengers appreciate.

Title: Anwar says court scrutiny can override secrecy of Pardons Board documents
Article:
SHENZHEN (China), Nov 19 — The original documents of the Pardons Board are classified as confidential, but their declassification is not unusual if they are challenged through court proceedings, said Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim.

He said applications or challenges through the courts involving such documents could normally lead to their declassification, while the date of implementation would be determined later.

“The original documents are indeed confidential, but usually, if they are brought to court, they are declassified. That was also the case in my previous case.

“They were initially classified, but once there was a court challenge. In my case, I did not challenge the Board’s decision; I challenged the process,” he told a press conference after attending the 2026 Apec Economic Leaders’ Meeting here today.

Anwar said any further questions or issues relating to the matter could be referred to the Cabinet.

He was commenting on reports concerning the minutes of a Federal Territories Pardons Board meeting, which discussed granting house arrest to former Prime Minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak and have since been declassified. — Bernama

Title: Johor halts Pontian land reclamation over suspected dumping of foreign construction waste
Article:
PONTIAN, Nov 19 — The Johor state government has ordered an immediate halt to land reclamation works at a project site suspected of using construction waste believed to have originated from a neighbouring country at Jalan Kampung Tenggayun, Mukim Rimba Terjun, here.

State Housing and Local Government Committee deputy chairman Zaidi Japar said the order was issued following the detection of various regulatory violations, including carrying out works without approval of Form B from the Pontian Municipal Council (MPPn) president.

He said the violations identified at the site, which had been active for the past week, included non-compliance with traffic management requirements, the installation of hoarding and signboards, waste management, and carrying out works without Form B approval.

“Johor is not a dumping ground for construction waste or a landfill. We are also concerned about technical safety, as the use of such materials could cause the piles to become unstable.

“In the future, this could potentially cause buildings to tilt, develop cracks and other structural problems,” he told reporters after inspecting the site at Mukim Rimba Terjun here today.

He said the contractor should have submitted Form B to MPPn president before commencing work, but the application was only submitted yesterday and has yet to receive approval.

He said apart from the closure order, legal action and fines could also be imposed depending on the offences, including carrying out works without approval.

He added that a report on the case would be submitted to the state executive council for further assessment, including possible follow-up action against the contractor.

“Stricter action will be taken as it is clear that they have disregarded the state government’s decision. This case will serve as an example to others,” he said.

Meanwhile, Johor SWCorp director Zainal Fitri Ahmad said no permit has been issued to allow construction waste from a neighbouring country to be brought into Malaysia. However, the authorities had detected the possibility of a loophole, with the waste believed to have been brought into the country using other permits.

Zainal Fitri said SWCorp is currently working with the Royal Malaysian Customs Department and the Natural Resources and Environmental Sustainability Ministry to investigate the matter.

He said SWCorp has records of vehicles entering the country, as well as information on the owners of the companies believed to be involved in the activity.

According to Zainal Fitri, the site is a newly identified location for such activities, and closure action would be taken to prevent them from continuing.

Those involved could also face legal action under the provisions of Act 672, in addition to being ordered to clean up the site and remove all construction waste dumped there, he added.

“A notice ordering the site to be cleaned up will be issued this week. We also want the dumped waste to be removed and the site restored to its original condition.

“The site owner has agreed to clean up the area, but we will monitor the implementation,” he said.

However, he stressed that SWCorp’s priority at present is to ensure that all locations used for illegal dumping are cleaned up and no longer used for such activities.

Yesterday, the media reported that 10 lorries linked to several companies had been detected during an enforcement operation at a reclamation site in Rimba Terjun here, which was suspected of being used to dump construction waste believed to have originated from a neighbouring country. — Bernama

Title: Chow Kon Yeow defends Penang’s RM8.4b water deal, says payments cover plant costs over 40 years
Article:
GEORGE TOWN, Nov 19 — The RM8.4 billion Capacity Charge payable over 40 years under the Bulk Water Supply Agreement (BWSA) between Penang and Perak represents deferred payments to recover the construction costs of a water treatment plant built specifically to supply water to Penang.

Penang Chief Minister Chow Kon Yeow said the charge, amounting to RM210 million annually, was an “availability payment” for the plant’s capacity.

It is a standard payment mechanism in long-term bulk water supply agreements and is separate from charges for the actual volume of water supplied, he said.

He explained that the water treatment plant, with a capacity of 500 million litres per day (MLD), was constructed exclusively to supply the Penang Water Supply Corporation (PBAPP), at an estimated construction cost of RM3 billion.

“When financing costs and plant renewal works over the 40 years are taken into account, the total amount comes to RM8.4 billion. This figure has undergone scrutiny and review by financial consultants appointed to conduct due diligence on the project.

“Prasarana Air dan Irigasi Perak (PAIP) is responsible for securing the financing and bearing the construction risks, while PBAPP is not required to make any upfront payments or capital contributions to PAIP,” he said in a statement today.

Yesterday, Bagan Member of Parliament Lim Guan Eng, who is also a former Penang Chief Minister, questioned why PBAPP was required to pay RM210 million annually for 40 years, amounting to RM8.4 billion, despite no treated water having been supplied to Penang to date.

Chow, who also chairs PBA Holdings Berhad (PBAHB) and PBAPP, explained that the plant’s construction costs would be recovered through the annual Capacity Charge over 40 years, beginning when water supply commences.

This arrangement, he said, would spread the financial commitment over the agreement’s duration, making the payments more manageable for PBAPP.

He added that the BWSA also provides for a separate Supply Charge, amounting to RM16.2 billion of the total RM24.6 billion payable under the agreement, which represents the cost of the water itself.

Addressing concerns raised by five PBAHB directors who had expressed reservations about certain aspects of the agreement, Chow said they generally acknowledged the need to secure the water supply but had raised concerns over the payment terms.

These concerns included the possible invocation of the “Perak State Interest Clause” and the implications of a prolonged suspension of water supply.

Chow stressed that several safeguards had been incorporated into the agreement to protect Penang’s interests, particularly those of PBAPP.

He said that under the agreement, PBAPP is only required to pay the Supply Charge based on the actual volume of water received that meets the stipulated quality standards.

Furthermore, PAIP is required to compensate PBAPP at an agreed rate for every cubic metre of water shortfall or supply that fails to meet the required quality standards, as verified by an independent laboratory.

He said PBAPP also retained the right to terminate the agreement and claim damages if PAIP breached its contractual obligations and failed to rectify the breach within 90 days.

In the event of a water supply suspension lasting more than three months, provided the disruption was not caused by PBAPP, either party would be entitled to request a renegotiation of the agreement. This could include referring the matter to their respective state governments for mediation.

“Either party may terminate the agreement only if the renegotiations fail to reach an agreement after a further three-month period.

“In such circumstances, PBAPP would only be required to make a one-off payment equivalent to the outstanding balance of the Capacity Charges, discounted at a rate of four per cent per annum, instead of continuing to pay RM210 million annually until 2072,” he explained.

Chow emphasised that the BWSA, which provides for a balanced allocation of risks between PBAPP and PAIP, was a strategic measure to secure Penang’s long-term water supply, particularly as the state’s existing surface water resources are projected to reach full utilisation by 2030. — Bernama

Title: KL prepares 86 classrooms for six-year-olds starting Year One in 2027
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 19 — A total of 86 classrooms at 48 schools in the Federal Territory of Kuala Lumpur have been prepared to accommodate six-year-old pupils entering Year One from 2027.

The Ministry of Education (MOE), through the Federal Territory of Kuala Lumpur Education Department (JPWPKL), said the classrooms were prepared using the “Modify and Upgrade” (USNT) approach and the Industrialised Building System (IBS).

“As of November 17, 2026, a total of 81 classrooms have been completed, while the remaining five, which are being constructed using the IBS method, are expected to be ready by the end of December 2026 at the latest,” the ministry said in a Facebook post today.

The ministry said the initiative was expected to benefit 3,820 pupils in three districts, namely Bangsar Pudu (45 schools), Keramat (25 schools) and Sentul (16 schools).

Meanwhile, the 2027 Academic Calendar for National Schools and Government-Aided Schools will run from January 4 to December 2, 2027, for schools in Group A states, and from January 4 to December 3, 2027, for those in Group B states.

Group A comprises Kedah, Kelantan and Terengganu, while Group B involves Johor, Melaka, Negeri Sembilan, Pahang, Perak, Perlis, Penang, Sabah, Sarawak, Selangor, the Federal Territories of Kuala Lumpur and Labuan, and Putrajaya. — Bernama

Title: Anwar calls for independent probe into Perak boarding school student’s death
Article:
SHENZHEN, Nov 19 — The death of a student at a boarding school in Perak should be a reminder to all parties of the importance of shared responsibility in ensuring the well-being of children, said Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim.

Anwar said he had discussed the incident with the police and Education Minister Datuk Seri Fadhlina Sidek, describing it as something he had never imagined could happen.

“This is a matter that deeply troubles us. May Allah SWT protect us and remind us all — parents, friends and peers — that this is an issue we must address together as one big Malaysian family,” he told a press conference after attending the 2026 Apec Economic Leaders’ Meeting here today.

As such, he called for a transparent and independent investigation rather than relying on existing departmental channels, to identify the actual cause of the incident.

He added that the investigation should examine the background and factors that led to the incident, including possible family issues, peer relationships or other aspects.

Anwar also questioned the supervision and care provided to students at boarding schools, particularly when students are absent from class or staying in areas such as the sick bay.

“In my experience, students at boarding schools are monitored. If they do not attend class, they are usually in the sick bay. Boarding schools have designated areas for students requiring care in the sick bay.

“But how come no one is assigned to look after the sick bay?” he said.

However, Anwar said it was important not to disclose excessive details regarding the incident out of respect for the victim’s family, while emphasising the importance of handling the matter with sensitivity. — Bernama

Title: Puchong chicken slaughterhouse to face Syariah, licensing charges next week
Article:
SHAH ALAM, Nov 19 — A premises in Puchong, suspected of operating as a non-Syariah-compliant chicken slaughtering and processing centre, is expected to face charges next week for several offences, including offences under the state’s Syariah enactment.

Selangor Islamic Religious Affairs and Cultural Innovation Committee chairman Dr Mohammad Fahmi Ngah said the premises, believed to have operated since 2004, will also face charges under local authority regulations, including licensing offences.

“As early as next week, the Puchong premises case will be up for mention and prosecution under both the local authority and the Syariah law enactment,” he said during the winding-up session of the Supply Enactment Bill 2026 at the Selangor State Legislative Assembly today.

Selangor Islamic Religious Council (Mais) chairman Datuk Salehuddin Saidin previously said the premises in Puchong, believed to be a chicken slaughtering, processing and distribution hub operating without a valid halal certificate, was found to use an electric water-bath stunning method in handling the poultry.

In addition, the Selangor Islamic Religious Department (Jais) seized more than 6.5 metric tonnes of raw chicken worth RM85,400, believed to have been processed without adhering to Islamic slaughtering methods, during an Ops Taring Chiller raid at a warehouse in Puchong at 12.40am on October 31. — Bernama

Title: Penang motorists face 221 days of diversions along Jalan Tun Dr Awang for LRT works
Article:
GEORGE TOWN, Nov 19 — Traffic diversions in both directions along Jalan Tun Dr Awang in Bayan Lepas will be in place for 221 days from November 21 to facilitate piling works and the construction of permanent structures for the Mutiara Line Light Rail Transit (LRT) project.

In a statement today, Malaysia Rapid Transit Corporation Sdn Bhd (MRT Corp) said the diversions would be in effect 24 hours a day until June 30, 2027.

“The diversions will cover sections of Jalan Tun Dr Awang from Kompleks Sri Relau to Sekolah Jenis Kebangsaan Cina (SJKC) Min Sin towards Komtar, and between Amari SPICE Hotel and the SPICE Aquatic Centre towards Bayan Lepas.

“The diversions are necessary to facilitate preliminary works for the Mutiara Line LRT project, involving piling and permanent structural works,” it said.

MRT Corp advised road users to exercise caution when passing through the affected areas. Eight traffic signs, along with traffic cones and flagmen, will be placed at the locations to assist with traffic control and ensure road users’ safety. — Bernama

Title: Baby girl found buried behind Pantai Remis home after suspected stabbing, mother and boyfriend held
Article:
IPOH, Nov 19 — A newborn baby girl, believed to have been stabbed by her biological mother, died in an incident in Pantai Remis on November 14.

Perak police chief Datuk Mohd Alwi Zainal Abidin said the incident is believed to have occurred on the day the baby was born, at about 1pm.

He said the initial investigation found that the baby’s mother, who is 19 years old, committed the act at her home before contacting her boyfriend to help bury the baby’s body behind her house.

This incident was uncovered after the baby’s mother told one of her friends about it.

“Her friend, feeling guilty, came forward to make a police report, which led to the investigation and the arrest of the victim’s mother and her boyfriend,” he said at a press conference at the Perak police contingent headquarters here today.

Mohd Alwi said that the initial investigation found two stab wounds on the baby’s chest, believed to have been made with a sharp weapon.

“We have obtained the weapon believed to have been used by the suspect in the incident,” he said, adding that both suspects have been remanded for six days since yesterday until Nov 23 to assist in the investigation under Section 302 of the Penal Code.

He added that the teenager would be sent for a psychiatric examination to determine the condition of her mental health. — Bernama

Title: Five new faces join Melaka exco as 10 assemblymen sworn in
Article:
MELAKA, Nov 19 — Ten state assemblymen, including five new faces, took their oaths of office today as members of the Melaka State Executive Council (Exco) here today.

The swearing-in ceremony was held before the Yang Dipertua Negeri of Melaka, Tun Mohd Ali Rustam, at Dewan Seri Utama, Melaka Governor’s Office, Seri Negeri, Ayer Keroh, at 2.45pm.

Also present at the swearing-in ceremony were the Governor’s wife, Toh Puan Asmah Abd Rahman, as well as Melaka Chief Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ab Rauf Yusoh and his wife, Datin Seri Zuriyah Ab Aziz.

Ab Rauf said the five new appointees were Ayer Molek assemblyman Datuk Mohd Ridhwan Mohd Ali, who will oversee the Education, Higher Education and TVET portfolio; Kelebang assemblyman Datuk Lim Ban Hong (Health and Human Capital); and Gadek assemblyman S. Nadarajah (Youth, Sports and NGOs).

“The other two are Rim assemblywoman Datuk Khaidhirah Abu Zahar (Women, Family and Community Development) and Bukit Katil assemblyman Muhammad Ridzuan Mohd Sarif (Agriculture, Environment and Disaster Management),” he told reporters after the ceremony here today.

Ab Rauf said the five executive councillors retained were Merlimau assemblyman Datuk Dr Muhammad Akmal Saleh (Science, Technology, Innovation and Digital Communications); Sungai Udang assemblyman Datuk Rais Yasin (Religion, Entrepreneur Development, Cooperatives and Cost of Living); and Telok Mas assemblyman Datuk Abdul Razak Abdul Rahman (Housing, Local Government and Rural Development).

“The others are Asahan assemblyman Datuk Dr Fairul Nizam Roslan (Tourism, Heritage, Culture and Unity) and Ayer Limau assemblyman Datuk Hameed Mytheen Kunju Basheer (Infrastructure, Transport and Utilities).

“Meanwhile, I will hold the portfolio for Economic Planning, Finance, Land, Investment and Industry,” he added.

In a related development, Ab Rauf said two assemblymen have been appointed deputy executive councillors for Economic Planning, Finance, Land, Investment and Industry, namely Duyong’s Datuk Mohd Noor Helmy Abdul Halem (Special Duties) and Machap Jaya’s Datuk Ngwe Hee Sem (Investment and Industry).

He said Rembia assemblyman Ahmad Norazril Abd Aziz has been appointed deputy executive councillor for Science, Technology, Innovation and Digital Communications; Lendu’s Datuk Abdul Hakim Abdul Wahid as deputy executive councillor for Religious Affairs, Entrepreneur Development, Cooperatives and Cost of Living; and Durian Tunggal assemblyman Datuk Dr Mustafa Musa as deputy executive councillor for Infrastructure, Transport and Utilities.

Others appointed as deputy executive councillors were Pengkalan Batu’s Siti Aisyah Mahmood (Women, Family and Community); Kuala Linggi’s Datuk Rosli Abdullah (Agriculture, Environment and Disaster Management); Sungai Rambai’s Jezlee Pit (Housing, Local Government and Rural Development);

Serkam’s Datuk Azman Abdullah (Tourism, Heritage, Culture and Unity); Pantai Kundor’s Datuk Tuminah Kadi @ Mohd Hashim (Education, Higher Education and TVET); Taboh Naning’s Datuk Zulkifli Mohd Zin (Health and Human Capital); and Paya Rumput’s Rafie Ahmad (Youth, Sports and NGOs).

Ab Rauf also announced the appointment of Bemban assemblyman Dr Mohd Yadzil Yaakub as Deputy Speaker of the Melaka State Legislative Assembly, with a decision on the post of Speaker to be made later.

At the 16th Melaka State election on Saturday (Nov 14), Barisan Nasional (BN) and Perikatan Nasional (PN) won 24 out of the 28 seats contested, enabling them to form the state government. — Bernama

Title: ‘Don’t be petty’: Anthony Loke tells Wee Ka Siong over ECRL launch approval concerns
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 19 — DAP secretary-general Anthony Loke has hit back at MCA president Datuk Seri Wee Ka Siong over concerns that the East Coast Rail Link (ECRL) launch could be held up by the absence of a Transport Minister, telling him not to be petty.

Responding to Wee’s remarks in the Dewan Rakyat, reported by The Star today, Loke said in a Facebook post that there were more pressing issues to address ahead of the December 12 launch of the railway’s first phase, including cable theft, signalling system readiness, crowd control and crisis management.

“My friend, this is the least of our worries!” he said, referring to the concern over the missing ministerial signature.

Wee had questioned whether the government had secured the necessary approval for the launch, saying the Land Public Transport Act 2010 requires the Transport Minister’s approval before a new railway system can begin operations.

He also asked whether the government had a contingency plan to obtain the approval in time, given that the launch is scheduled in about three weeks.

Deputy Transport Minister Datuk Hasbi Habibollah acknowledged in Parliament that the minister’s signature was required, but said he was confident the government would address the matter and noted that a new minister could be appointed within a week.

Loke, who tendered his resignation as Transport Minister on November 10, said the Prime Minister could assume responsibility for a ministry without a minister or appoint another Cabinet member to temporarily carry out its duties.

He said this authority was provided for under Article 39 of the Federal Constitution.

Loke also urged Wee to have greater confidence in the Transport Ministry’s secretary-general and legal adviser.

“Don’t be too petty la, please,” he added.

The ECRL’s first phase covers the 523km route between Kota Bharu in Kelantan and Gombak in Selangor, with passenger services scheduled to begin on December 12.

Title: Setia Alam landslide: Road near Sri Pinang Apartments closed, no casualties
Article:
SHAH ALAM, Nov 19 — A landslide on the hillside near the Sri Pinang Apartments on Persiaran Setia Makmur, Setia Alam, here today was reported to not involve any casualties.

The Selangor branch of the Malaysian Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM) assistant director of operations Ashrul Riezal Asbar said in a statement that his team rushed to the scene after receiving an emergency call today at 11.30am.

He said the operation involved a team of seven officers and members along with machinery from the Klang Selatan Fire and Rescue Station (BBP).

“Upon arrival at the location, the inspection found that a landslide had occurred on the hillside of the area.

“The ground condition was found to be static and the incident did not involve any victims or buildings,” he said, adding that further action was then handed over to the local authorities (PBT) and the police.

Meanwhile, the Shah Alam City Council (MBSA) announced through a post on the Threads application that the road in that area has been temporarily closed for safety reasons.
