The post said that safety ropes and barriers have been installed around the affected area to prevent road users from entering the risk zone.

“Warning signs were also placed to inform road users about the incident and the closure of the route.

“Following that, road users are advised to always be cautious, adhere to road closure instructions, and use alternative routes during the closure period,” according to the post.

Earlier, the incident went viral on social media through videos and images showing the road in the area being closed as a safety measure, with authorities controlling the situation. — Bernama

Title: No protection for chicken abattoirs flouting halal rules, Selangor says
Article:
SHAH ALAM, Nov 19 — The Selangor state government will not shield any company found to have violated regulations relating to suspected non-compliance with Islamic slaughtering requirements at chicken abattoirs, but will withhold the identities of those involved to avoid any allegation of mala fide (bad faith).

State Islamic Affairs and Innovation Culture Committee chairman Dr Mohammad Fahmi Ngah said the move was intended to respect the investigation process and subsequent legal proceedings involving 11 unlicensed chicken slaughtering and processing premises in the state.

He said the identities of those involved should only be disclosed once the cases went to court to avoid embarrassing individuals or triggering legal implications.

“It is not a matter of us being afraid or wanting to shield anyone. Naming companies or individuals carries legal implications. We have to consider the appropriate legal aspects, unless the court has already disclosed their identities.

“Let the court make the official announcement so that no malicious assumptions arise, as we must not have any mala fide before the cases begin,” he said.

He was speaking at the announcement of the Selangor Islamic Religious Department’s (Jais) Primary School Religious Assessment (PSRA) results, which was also attended by Jais director Datuk Mohd Shahzihan Ahmad.

Mohammad Fahmi said the 11 premises without certified slaughterers comprised one case in Puchong, five premises previously subjected to enforcement action and another five newly identified through a recent review of local authorities’ inventories.

He said coordinated enforcement operations had begun, with items seized and closure notices issued to immediately halt chicken processing activities at the premises. The investigation papers for the Puchong case were also nearly complete and expected to be mentioned in court early next week.

“My concern is not only halal compliance, but also unlicensed premises and failure to meet health requirements. The consumption of chicken is not just about whether it is halal, we must also ensure that it is safe in every respect, including being free from disease.

“The chicken may be halal, but if hygiene and food safety requirements are not met, then I believe it should not be consumed by Muslims or non-Muslims in Selangor,” he said.

Meanwhile, he said investigations had been widened through cross-checks between Jais and local authority databases in each district. The authorities also welcomed information and complaints from the public, including those shared on social media platforms such as Facebook.

He said one or two cases had so far been detected under each relevant local authority, with the authorities awaiting full feedback on enforcement action against the five newly identified premises. — Bernama

Title: Perak police rule out foul play in death of Form Three student at Kuala Kangsar boarding school
Article:
IPOH, Nov 19 — The Form Three student found dead at a boarding school in Kuala Kangsar yesterday died from neck constriction, police said.

Perak Police chief Datuk Mohd Alwi Zainal Abidin said the cause of death was established following a post-mortem examination conducted at the Forensic Medicine Department of Taiping Hospital today.

He said investigations found no evidence of foul play or bullying in connection with the student’s death.

“The student’s death has been classified as a sudden death report (SDR),” he told a press conference at the Perak Police Contingent headquarters here.

Mohd Alwi said police had recorded statements from 13 people, including the student’s parents, teachers and schoolmates, and would continue taking statements from other relevant parties as necessary. — Bernama

Title: Police hunt four gang members after robbery mastermind killed in Ipoh shootout
Article:
IPOH, Nov 19 — Police have launched an intensive manhunt for four fugitives after the alleged mastermind of a violent interstate robbery syndicate was shot dead in a gun battle with detectives in Ipoh early today.

The deceased suspect, a 39-year-old Malaysian carrying 17 prior criminal records, was killed along Jalan Persiaran Lembah Perpaduan around 2.30am after opening fire on a joint surveillance team comprising Bukit Aman and Perak Criminal Investigation Department (CID) personnel.

Addressing a press conference at the Perak police headquarters today, Bukit Aman CID director Datuk M. Kumar detailed how the tactical intercept unfolded.

“Police spotted a silver Perodua Alza being driven suspiciously and approached the vehicle before identifying themselves as police officers and ordering the driver to stop.

“However, he failed to comply and sped off in a manner that endangered other road users. Police pursued and intercepted the vehicle, resulting in a minor collision which forced it to stop,” he said during a press conference here today.

Kumar said the driver exited the car and unleashed multiple shots at the pursuing officers in a bid to escape into the darkness.

“Police were forced to return fire as the suspect posed a threat to the lives of the officers. Once the situation was brought under control and deemed safe, checks were carried out,” he said.

Kumar underscored that the raiding team exercised proportionate lethal force only when confronted with mortal peril.

“We only go to that limit when our lives are threatened. When we have no other choice, that will be the last resort,” he added.

The suspect was discovered dead near a roadside drain. Forensic investigators recovered a semi-automatic handgun, three live rounds, and six spent shell casings beside his body, alongside a packet containing crystalline powder suspected to be methamphetamine.

A search of the impounded vehicle uncovered an extensive burglary arsenal, including three machetes, two crowbars, a metal cutter, two face masks, two pairs of gloves, vehicle registration plates, cables, car keys, and additional packets of methamphetamine.

Kumar disclosed that the deceased, who had no record of formal employment, was wanted for an extensive criminal history spanning armed robbery, housebreaking, narcotics, and inflicting grievous bodily harm. Detectives have identified four surviving core members of the syndicate who remain at large, while another accomplice was picked up recently in connection with a separate home invasion in Tanjung Malim.

“The arrested suspect is an additional suspect, while we are looking for these four others,” he said.

The gang had actively terrorised residential neighbourhoods across Perak, Selangor, Penang, and Melaka for roughly a year since 2025, with investigators linking the network to at least 22 cases involving violent home robberies, extortion, and assault.

“The group is connected, but the members are not related to each other. They operate in groups of four or five during each robbery.

“They are dangerous as they have firearms and machetes and are aggressive. They will not hesitate to injure their victims,” he said.

Kumar explained that the syndicate's operational strategy involved targeting landed homes located in close proximity to major expressways, allowing them to stage blitz break-ins and execute rapid interstate getaways before authorities could seal escape routes.

“They would first conduct surveillance and reconnaissance, visiting the areas several times before carrying out the robbery. During the robberies, they would wear masks to prevent identification,” he said.

The investigation is proceeding under Section 307 of the Penal Code for attempted murder and Section 3 of the Firearms (Increased Penalties) Act 1971, which mandates the death penalty for discharging a firearm during the commission of a scheduled crime.

Title: Malaysian govt weighs changes to drug law to shift focus from punishment to rehabilitation
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR، Nov 19 — The government is willing to consider a review of Section 15(1) of the Dangerous Drugs Act 1952 as part of efforts to enhance drug treatment and rehabilitation، as drug-related offences account for nearly half of all convicted prisoners in the country.

Deputy Home Minister Datuk Seri Dr Shamsul Anuar Nasarah said the government acknowledged the proposal and was willing to evaluate the effectiveness of existing laws in light of current data and on-the-ground experience.

“The figures speak volumes. In view of this، the government has noted the suggestion to review Section 15(1) of the Dangerous Drugs Act 1952.

“The government is committed to reviewing the effectiveness of laws based on available data and experience on the ground، while ensuring the continued protection of public safety and order، ” he said during the question-and-answer session in the Dewan Rakyat today.

He was responding to a supplementary question from Wong Shu Qi (PH-Kluang)، who asked the government to consider amending Section 15(1) of the Act and issuing guidelines to prosecutors and magistrates to divert drug addicts to rehabilitation centres from the time of arrest to address prison overcrowding.

Wong said the measure was important amid a rise in the prison population from 83,944 in January to around 90,000 in October this year، with many of the cases linked to drug offences، despite amendments to the Drug Dependants (Treatment and Rehabilitation) Act 1983 [Act 283] having come into effect on August 22,2025.

Shamsul Anuar explained that the amendments to Act 283 were intended to shift the approach from imprisonment to treatment and rehabilitation، without completely abolishing criminal offences related to drugs or removing them from the criminal justice framework.

He said that between January and September this year، 12,255 prisoners were serving sentences for taking drugs under Section 15(1)(a) of the Dangerous Drugs Act 1952، while another 31,827 were serving sentences for possessing small amounts of drugs.

“Combined، the two groups represent 46.5 per cent of the total 94,780 sentenced prisoners currently in the country’s prisons، ” he said.

He said the Dangerous Drugs Act 1952 falls under the Health Ministry، and its implementation involves two key agencies under the Home Ministry: the police for enforcement and the National Anti-Drug Agency for prevention، treatment and rehabilitation.

He said the integration of law enforcement and public health efforts facilitated the early detection of drug addiction cases، allowing individuals to be referred to rehabilitation programmes، including through court orders. — Bernama

Title: From green spaces to elder care, Hannah Yeoh outlines what makes a prosperous KL
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR، Nov 19 — Wealth should not just be accumulated but also enjoyed and shared with others، Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Federal Territories) Hannah Yeoh said today.

Financial prosperity، according to her، should be balanced with quality of life and social responsibility، with a strong economy and liveable city providing the foundation for people to prosper and contribute meaningfully to society.

Speaking at the official opening of HSBC Wealth Centre here today، Yeoh said the government’s priority was to strengthen the Malaysian economy to ensure that prosperity could be enjoyed by all، stressing that economic growth remained fundamental to the country’s progress.

She said Kuala Lumpur was also focusing on creating a liveable urban environment for people to enjoy their wealth and quality of life، including protecting green spaces، reducing flash flood risks، improving connectivity and preserving the city’s heritage.

“I want to assure all of you that when the Madani Government says we are serious about improving the economy، we really mean it because we want everyone to prosper.

“That is why، in Kuala Lumpur، we are putting a lot of effort into protecting our green spaces، which my single priority this year is to make sure that we protect and preserve our parks and green spaces، ” she said.

She noted that among the initiatives were efforts to gazette parks، develop 32 green spaces under the microforest concept by 2027 and plan 22 kilometres of covered pedestrian walkways across all 11 parliamentary constituencies in Kuala Lumpur under Budget 2027.

Yeoh said the city was also investing in flood mitigation measures and working towards becoming a Sponge City، with flood hotspots reduced from more than 30 in 2022 to 14 currently، and a target of bringing the number down to 10 by year-end.

She said prosperity should also be shared with those less fortunate، citing Kuala Lumpur City Hall’s (DBKL) provision of free school bus services for children from low-income families living in public housing communities as one example of how public resources could help improve access to education.

Yeoh also called for businesses to look beyond conventional markets and recognise emerging opportunities arising from changing lifestyles، demographics and consumer needs، particularly among senior citizens.

She said older people needed more than healthcare and physical activities، but also companionship، social interaction and meaningful programmes، presenting opportunities for services and platforms tailored to their needs.

Drawing from her experience as Youth and Sports Minister، Yeoh said institutions and businesses must be willing to rethink conventional approaches and adapt to changing circumstances، citing Malaysia’s improved overall medal haul at the 2025 SEA Games in Thailand as an example of the benefits of embracing a different strategy.

She said Malaysia returned from the Games with 231 medals، its highest-ever total at a SEA Games held outside Kuala Lumpur، after shifting away from publicly announcing separate gold، silver and bronze medal targets to focusing on the overall medal count.

Yeoh said the same willingness to adapt was needed in the business sector، as the way people earn، spend and plan for retirement continued to evolve، creating new opportunities for businesses to serve different segments of society.

She urged the society to continue supporting efforts to build a safe، stable and prosperous nation where people of all backgrounds had opportunities to grow، enjoy their wealth and contribute towards the well-being of others.

“To achieve all of that، we need a strong economy، a liveable city and a society where everyone has an opportunity to progress، ” she also said.

Located at Jalan P Ramlee in the heart of Kuala Lumpur’s Golden Triangle، the HSBC Wealth Centre is the bank’s third wealth centre in Malaysia and second in Kuala Lumpur، following its flagship centre at Tun Razak Exchange (TRX) and another in Johor Bahru.

Also present at the event were HSBC Bank Malaysia chief executive officer Datuk Omar Siddiq and country head of international wealth and premier banking Linda Yip. — Bernama

Title: Pontian fire damages 100m of conveyor belts linking jetty to coal storage
Article:
PONTIAN, Nov 19 — A midday fire damaged three industrial rubber conveyor belts connecting the marine jetty to the coal storage facility at the Tanjung Bin Energy power complex in Kukup today.

Firefighters were alerted to the emergency at 11.39am, prompting an immediate deployment from the Pontian Baru Fire and Rescue Station, operations commander Mohd Hasnan Abd Rahman said in a statement.

“Following the call, 13 personnel supported by a Fire Rescue Tender (FRT), a Compact Fire Rescue Tender (CFRT), and a Hilux four-wheel-drive vehicle were immediately dispatched to the scene.

“Upon arrival, the team discovered a fire had damaged three rubber conveyor belts, spanning approximately 100 metres, which connect the jetty to the Malakoff Tanjung Bin coal storage facility.

“The operation was divided into five sectors and firemen also carried out containment efforts on both the left and right sides to prevent the blaze from spreading further,” he said.

The fire fighting effort was reinforced by 20 on-site personnel from plant operator Malakoff Corporation Bhd, alongside a 10-member joint contingent from the facility’s internal Emergency Response Team and the Port of Tanjung Pelepas (PTP) fire service.

Responding crews deployed two 90-metre hose lines equipped with four breeching units and eight branch nozzles, drafting water from two nearby high-pressure hydrants to douse the conveyor alignment.

“The fire was brought under control at 1.28pm and operations are currently still ongoing,” Mohd Hasnan confirmed.

Authorities reported no casualties or injuries arising from the incident, and fire investigation forensic teams are currently establishing the cause and origin of the blaze.

Title: Home minister: Malaysia, China step up cooperation against cross-border crime, cyber fraud
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR، Nov 19 — Malaysia and China will continue to strengthen bilateral cooperation in security and law enforcement، particularly in addressing increasingly complex cross-border crime threats.

Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said the commitment was reaffirmed during his meeting with China’s State Councilor and Minister of Public Security Wang Xiaohong in Shenzhen، China، yesterday.

He said the meeting، which received extensive coverage in China’s major media outlets، also focused on efforts to tackle telecommunications and cyber fraud.

“We also discussed efforts to intensify joint operations، strengthen cooperation in strategic areas and advance international initiatives to combat telecommunications and cyber fraud، ” he said in a Facebook post today.

Saifuddin Nasution said the historic meeting also saw the signing of relevant cooperation documents as part of the ongoing commitment between the two countries.

He described security cooperation as crucial to ensuring the safety and well-being of the people of both countries.

“Malaysia and China enjoy close bilateral relations. Security cooperation is important not only to strengthen strategic ties، but more importantly، to ensure the safety and well-being of our people، ” he said.

Saifuddin Nasution was part of Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim’s official delegation to China for the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (Apec) Summit. — Bernama

Title: Fahmi: Malaysia to test emergency alert system near Parliament on Nov 23, nationwide on Nov 29
Article:
PUTRAJAYA، Nov 19 — Malaysia’s national emergency early warning system (EWS) will undergo a simulation test in the vicinity of Parliament on November 23، followed by a nationwide test on November 29.

Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) would issue public service announcements (PSAs) to inform the public about the alert messages and sounds they would receive on their mobile phones.

He said the simulation test was aimed at ensuring that people understood the notifications were part of a system test and not actual emergency alerts.

“We will also arrange for these public service announcements to be aired in cinemas and on television and radio. We will work with social media influencers and platforms such as TikTok to raise public awareness of the early warning system، ” he told reporters after the Communications Ministry’s monthly assembly here today.

Fahmi said users would not need to download or install any applications، as the system would send alerts directly to compatible mobile phones.

He said the system would complement existing warning methods، including short message service (SMS) alerts and sirens installed along rivers by the Department of Irrigation and Drainage (DID).

“Users with older mobile phones will continue to receive SMS alerts، while those with newer phones will receive EWS alerts as pop-up messages.

“There is no need to install or download any application، as the system communicates directly with mobile phones rather than through SMS، ” he said.

Fahmi said the EWS could be used not only to warn the public about natural disasters such as floods، landslides and earthquakes، but also to address public safety and security concerns.

He said the Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM) or the National Security Council (NSC) could use the system to share important information with the public، including alerts about missing persons or children.

“For example، if someone goes missing in a particular area and cannot be located، the system could be used to alert people in that area. The same applies to missing children، as practised in several other countries that use similar alert systems.

“We see its potential not only for natural disasters، including floods، landslides and earthquakes، but also for public safety and security matters.

“The EWS is location-based. When an incident occurs in a particular area، the alert will reach everyone within that area. However، because the alerts are broadcast more generally، people in unaffected locations may also receive them، ” he said.

On flood warning messages circulated through WhatsApp recently، Fahmi clarified that they were not part of the EWS implementation، as the system delivers alerts through pop-up notifications rather than SMS or WhatsApp. — Bernama

Title: Police link man killed in Chow Kit shootout to string of armed robberies
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 19 — The man who was shot dead in an exchange of gunfire with police in Chow Kit here early yesterday is believed to have been involved in a series of robberies since early May and linked to nine separate cases.

Kuala Lumpur police chief Datuk Fadil Marsus said the nine cases were identified after the victims recognised the suspect, helping investigators establish his alleged involvement in the crimes.

He added that police were continuing investigations to identify and track down other individuals believed to be connected to the suspect’s criminal activities.

“We believe the suspect also used other vehicles to carry out the robberies, although a detailed investigation is still underway.

“Kuala Lumpur police are confident that we will be able to uncover the network and identify individuals who conspired with the main suspect,” he told a press conference following a case exhibits disposal ceremony organised by the Kuala Lumpur Police Contingent Headquarters’ Criminal Investigation Department at the Alam Damai Police Post here today.

Fadil said the suspect was believed to have specifically targeted women and elderly individuals in the robberies.

The man, in his 30s, was also believed to have used a taxi stolen in Gombak last October to rob a foreign woman and an elderly man.

In the incident at about 2 am yesterday, a team from the Special Investigation Division (D9) of the Criminal Investigation Department (CID), comprising personnel from the Kuala Lumpur Police Contingent Headquarters and Bukit Aman, raided a room in a shophouse in Chow Kit.

The suspect allegedly fired several shots at the police during the raid, prompting an exchange of gunfire in which he was shot dead.

Police also seized a firearm and suspected crystal methamphetamine (syabu) from the room.

The case is being investigated under Sections 392 and 397 of the Penal Code. — Bernama

Title: ‘All I want is a transparent probe’: Father breaks silence on son’s death in Perak school
Article:
TAIPING, Nov 19 — The father of a Form Three student who was found dead at a school in Perak has called for a transparent and thorough investigation to establish the circumstances surrounding his son’s death.

Mohd Idzwan Razali, 48, said he was remaining calm and leaving it to the authorities to determine the actual cause of the incident.

“A transparent and thorough investigation...that is what I hope for. The school has provided an explanation, but it remains subject to the findings of the investigation,” he told reporters when met at the Forensic Medicine Department of Taiping Hospital today.

Mohd Idzwan, who is self-employed, said he was informed of the incident involving his third child of five by the police and the school principal yesterday evening.

Describing his late son, who had been studying at the boarding school since Form One, as a well-behaved boy, he said the teenager had led an ordinary school life like his peers.

He said their last meeting was during the recent Deepavali holidays, when his son travelled by bus to his wife’s family home in Kuala Pilah, Negeri Sembilan.

He added that they had also exchanged messages on Telegram about family matters shortly before the incident.

Mohd Idzwan, who resides in Kuala Lumpur, said his son’s remains were expected to be buried in Juasseh, Negeri Sembilan, after the post-mortem examination was completed today.

Last night, the Perak Education Department confirmed that a Form Three student had been found dead at a school in the state.

Following the incident, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim called for a thorough and transparent investigation to establish the actual cause of the student’s death. — Bernama

Title: Johor Baru police probe viral video of boy hit by car near school
Article:
JOHOR BAHRU، Nov 19 — Police have initiated investigations into a social media video where a young boy was injured after being hit by a car in front of a school in Bandar Baru Uda here yesterday.

The incident، involving a black Perodua Myvi، was captured on a close-circuit television (CCTV) camera before the video footage was posted on various social media platforms.

The 12-year-old boy sustained serious injuries to his head، arms، and legs، while the driver was unharmed.

Johor Bahru North police chief Assistant Commissioner Azrol Anuar Nor said that authorities were alerted of the 12-second video that was uploaded on the Threads platform.

“Initial investigations showed that the incident occurred as the car، driven by a 70-year-old man، was travelling in the leftmost lane from the direction of the city centre toward Jalan Jagong at 5.30pm.

“Upon reaching the scene، the boy then darted across the road from the left side to the right.

“The driver was unable to avoid the child and struck him، ” he said in a statement today.

Azrol Anuar said the injured boy was rushed to the Sultanah Aminah Hospital (HSA) for medical treatment.

He said the driver did not sustain any injuries.

The case is being investigated under Section 43(1) of the Road Transport Act 1987 for careless and inconsiderate driving that resulted in an accident.

The driver faces a fine of between RM5,000 and RM10,000، as well as a potential prison sentence of up to a year upon conviction.

Azrol Anuar advised motorists to remain vigilant and slow down، especially when passing through school zones and pedestrian crossings.

“Parents and guardians are also reminded to keep a close watch on their children when they are crossing the road to prevent any untoward incidents، ” he said.

Title: ‘See you tomorrow’: Negeri Sembilan MB Ismail Lasim keeps reporters guessing amid resignation uncertainty
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR، Nov 19 — Negeri Sembilan Mentri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim has left reporters guessing about his political future after repeatedly telling them to meet him the following day when questioned about his position amid uncertainty over his resignation.

The Star reported that Ismail remained cheerful when approached after launching the state-level Zakat Month today، brushing aside questions as he left the venue.

Asked whether he was scheduled to have an audience with Yang di-Pertuan Besar Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir tomorrow، Ismail laughed before once again telling reporters: “Jumpa esok” (See you tomorrow).

He also declined to disclose where reporters could find him، suggesting they would be able to work it out themselves.

“You have not seen me for four days، but you guys are smart enough and would know where to find me، ” he said.

Asked how he was doing after several days away from public view، Ismail replied: “Alhamdullilah، I’m doing alright.”

The latest exchange comes amid uncertainty over the status of his resignation، which Barisan Nasional secretary-general Datuk Seri Zambry Abdul Kadir announced in a statement on November 16.

Zambry said coalition chairman Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi، who is also Umno president، had received a copy of Ismail’s resignation letter dated November 16 and addressed to Tuanku Muhriz.

However، the Negri Sembilan Palace said the following day that Ismail remained the menteri besar pending royal assent، explaining that a resignation would only take effect once accepted by the Ruler in accordance with the state constitution.

Ahmad Zahid subsequently confirmed that Barisan had submitted one candidate for the position to Tuanku Muhriz on November 16، adding that the decision to approve and announce the appointment rested with the Ruler.

He also rejected claims that Umno was interfering in the state’s affairs، saying the nomination followed constitutional conventions and adat after Ismail، who is also Juasseh assemblyman، voluntarily tendered his resignation just four months after taking office.

Meanwhile، Ismail’s son Naim questioned Barisan’s announcement، saying it had yet to be confirmed by the palace and asking in an Instagram post whether his father had personally issued the statement or whether it had been made on his behalf.

Ismail was sworn in as menteri besar on August 2.

Title: Update your phones to receive Malaysia’s new emergency alerts, MCMC tells public
Article:
CYBERJAYA، Nov 19 — Malaysians have been urged to update their mobile phone operating systems to ensure their devices can receive emergency notifications under the country’s new Early Warning System (EWS)، which is being rolled out in stages.

The Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) said the system uses Cell Broadcast System (CBS) technology to send alerts simultaneously to compatible mobile phones within designated geographical areas، without requiring users to download an application، register or subscribe to a dedicated service.

As an initial guide، devices expected to support EWS alerts include Apple iPhone 11 and newer models running iOS 27.2 or later، Android phones operating on Android 12 or later، and Huawei devices using EMUI 16 or later، subject to final technical confirmation.

Users are also advised to install the latest software updates available for their devices، restart their phones after updating and ensure emergency alert settings are enabled، where applicable.

In a statement، MCMC said it had held a special briefing with media editors-in-chief today to introduce the EWS، explain how alerts would be delivered and strengthen media cooperation in raising public awareness and disaster preparedness.

The session included a demonstration conducted through an internal technical test at the commission’s building in Cyberjaya.

MCMC clarified that the activity on November 19 was an internal technical test to evaluate and improve the system ahead of its wider implementation، with larger-scale testing to be conducted in stages.

The EWS is being developed through cooperation between MCMC، the National Disaster Management Agency (Nadma)، relevant technical agencies and telecommunications service providers to strengthen the country’s ability to deliver emergency warnings more quickly and accurately.

The public has been reminded to stay alert to official information and follow instructions from the authorities when emergency alerts are received.

MCMC said the EWS would complement existing warning channels as part of broader efforts to improve public safety and preparedness in dealing with disasters.

Title: Selangor records 439 TNB cable theft cases since 2023, losses hit RM62.7m
Article:
SHAH ALAM, Nov 19 — A total of 439 cable theft cases involving Tenaga Nasional Berhad (TNB) assets were recorded in Selangor from Jan 1, 2023 to Sept 30 this year, resulting in losses amounting to RM62.7 million.

State Infrastructure and Agriculture Committee chairman Datuk Izham Hashim said 166 cases were recorded between Jan 1 and Sept 30 this year alone, with Cheras recording the highest number at 45, followed by Bangi (37), Port Klang (24), Banting (12) and Rawang (10).

Meanwhile, Izham said the Selangor Department of Irrigation and Drainage (DID) recorded 38 cases of cable and equipment theft at pump houses and water gates between 2023 and 2026, involving losses estimated at RM1.5 million.

“Klang district recorded the highest losses at RM667,000 involving eight cases, followed by Kuala Langat (17 cases, RM499,000), Kuala Selangor (10 cases, RM318,000) and Sepang (three cases, RM47,000),” he said during the State Legislative Assembly sitting today.

Izham said this in his reply to a question from Jefri Mejan (PN-Ijok), who wanted to know the number of cable theft cases involving the Public Works Department (JKR) and TNB recorded in Selangor since 2023, as well as the losses incurred by district.

He added that the JKR also suffered estimated losses of between RM50,000 and RM100,000 per month for each cable theft incident reported across the state’s nine districts.

Title: Home Ministry purges 36 errant Immigration staff linked to pass scam
Article:
KUALA
LUMPUR, Nov 19 — A total of 36 officers and staff members of the
Immigration Department of Malaysia (JIM) have been arrested,
suspended from duty or charged in court over their suspected
involvement in a syndicate issuing fraudulent medical passes and
Temporary Employment Visit Passes (PLKS) between 2025 and the middle
of this year.

Deputy Home Minister Datuk
Seri Dr Shamsul Anuar Nasarah said the Home Ministry (KDN) would not
compromise on matters involving integrity, adding that several
special operations had been conducted in collaboration with the
Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) to address internal
misconduct and corruption.

He said the digitalisation
of the PLKS through the full implementation of the electronic
Temporary Employment Visit Pass (ePLKS) system, which eliminates the
need for physical stickers, had also helped curb the forgery of
employment-related documents.

“The full implementation
of the ePLKS system, which eliminates physical stickers and is
integrated with a biometric system, has indeed yielded positive
results.

“The counterfeiting of
physical stickers by illegal printing operations has been reduced by
nearly 90 per cent as of 2026. This is because verification can now
be carried out digitally in the field using smart devices to scan a
centralised QR code that cannot be duplicated,” he said during the
question-and-answer session in the Dewan Rakyat today.

He was responding to a
supplementary question from Manndzri Nasib (BN-Tenggara), who sought
an update on KDN’s internal cleansing operations, conducted in
collaboration with MACC, to identify and take action against
officials suspected of colluding with syndicates.

Manndzri also asked about
the effectiveness of the PLKS digitalisation initiative in 2026 in
addressing loopholes that had enabled the forgery of employment
documents.

Earlier, in response to an
original question from Syed Saddiq Syed Abdul Rahman (MUDA-Muar) on
the breakdown of undocumented foreign nationals and enforcement
efforts, Shamsul Anuar said JIM had arrested 35,109 foreign nationals
during enforcement operations between Jan 1 and Sept 15 this year.

During the same period,
another 22,495 foreign nationals were handed over to the authorities
at entry points or by other enforcement agencies, including the Royal
Malaysia Police (PDRM), bringing the combined total of arrests and
handovers to 57,604.

He said Indonesian
nationals accounted for the largest number, at 16,744, followed by
Bangladeshis (13,543) and Myanmar nationals (8,452).

Meanwhile, a total of
41,277 foreign nationals had been deported to their respective
countries after completing the necessary documentation processes.

Shamsul Anuar also said
that 304,905 undocumented foreign nationals had registered under the
Migrant Repatriation Programme 2.0 as of Sept 15, of whom 243,463 had
voluntarily returned to their home countries. — Bernama

Title: WhatsApp group misunderstanding sparked Johor school assault initially suspected to be bullying, say police
Article:
TANGKAK, Nov 19 — A misunderstanding in a WhatsApp group is believed to have triggered the assault of a 14-year-old boy by three older students at a secondary school in Johor on November 13, police said today.

The incident, which was shared on Facebook, was initially suspected to be a case of bullying involving students at a secondary school in Parit Bunga, Tangkak.

Tangkak police chief Superintendent Roslan Mohd Talib said police were alerted to the incident after a report was lodged the following day.

“Preliminary investigations indicate that the incident occurred inside a classroom and at the secondary school’s pavilion at 8am on November 13.

“The victim alleged that he was repeatedly kicked and punched by the three suspects on various parts of his body.

“As a result, the victim sought treatment at the Sultanah Fatimah Specialist Hospital (HPSF) in Muar, where he sustained soft tissue injuries to the left side of his head, chest, abdomen and left arm,” he said in a statement today.

Roslan said police subsequently identified and detained three 15-year-old boys to assist with the investigation.

He added that all three admitted their involvement during initial questioning.

“Investigators have classified the incident under Section 323 of the Penal Code for voluntarily causing hurt.

“The police take any form of bullying or violence involving students very seriously. Resorting to physical force to resolve issues is unacceptable, as it compromises the safety of the victim,” he said.

Roslan urged parents and school authorities to monitor students’ social interactions and take complaints of bullying seriously.

He also advised the public against speculating or sharing information that could reveal the identities of the students involved, all of whom are minors.

Meanwhile, Johor Education and Information Committee chairman Muhammad Naqib Md Ghazali called for a transparent and thorough police investigation.

He expressed hope that the investigation would be conducted without outside interference to ensure justice for all parties.

“At the same time, I also request that the school and the Johor education department (JPNJ) take follow-up measures regarding the incident,” he told reporters at the Johor state legislative assembly in Kota Iskandar, Iskandar Puteri, during the tabling of the Johor Budget 2027.

Two video clips of the alleged assault had earlier circulated on social media.

One showed a student punching and kicking another student, while the other showed a group of students making obscene gestures inside a classroom.

The social media post also included a letter from HPSF confirming that the victim had sustained injuries following the incident.

Title: BN lawmakers call for internal audit, police probe over leaked Najib pardon papers
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 19 — Several Barisan Nasional federal lawmakers today urged the public “to lodge as many police reports as possible”, as they called on the authorities to investigate who leaked the Federal Territories Pardons Board minutes that discussed Datuk Seri Najib Razak’s conditional pardon.

The members of parliament also called on Chief Secretary to the Government Tan Sri Shamsul Azri Abu Bakar to conduct an internal audit to snuff out the parties they claimed had violated the Official Secrets Act.

The MPs honed in on former DAP lawmaker Tony Pua and news portal Malaysiakini, whom they suggested were the first to have shared the leaked minutes on the internet. The government has yet to confirm their authenticity, but copies of the minutes are already being widely circulated online.

“We urge the Legal Affairs Division (BHEUU) of the Prime Minister’s Department and the Attorney General’s Chambers (AGC) to issue an official statement within 24 hours to verify the authenticity of the document in question as well as its legal classification status,” Datuk Shamshulkahar Mohd Deli (BN-Jempol) said at a press conference in Parliament here.

“Second, urging the Chief Secretary to the Government (KSN) to conduct an immediate security audit and internal investigation to identify the mastermind behind this leak of confidential government information,” the MPs added.

“Third, urging the Royal Malaysia Police to open a comprehensive investigation paper, without fear or favour, against the individuals who disseminated the document.”

Umno leaders have called the leaking of the minutes partisan political polemic, as they condemned the action as an attempt to stain the Royal Institution.

Yesterday Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said asserted that the proposal to declassify the minutes was discussed at last week’s Cabinet meeting “indirectly”, meaning there was no decision to make them public.

Umno has questioned if the minutes were published legally, noting that declassifying any officially classified documents would require that specific steps be taken.

Title: Onn Hafiz thanks Anwar for RM4.86b federal allocation for Johor projects
Article:
ISKANDAR PUTERI, Nov 19 — The Johor State Government expressed its appreciation to the Federal Government, particularly to Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim, for the allocation of RM4.86 billion through the second rolling plan of the 2027 13th Malaysia Plan (13MP).

Johor Menteri Besar Datuk Onn Hafiz Ghazi said the allocation would help realise Johor’s development aspirations on a larger scale.

He said the allocation involves a total of 94 new projects and 515 continuation projects in the state.

Onn Hafiz said the projects included the upgrading of Route FT003 Kota Tinggi-Mersing Road from Section 35.5 to Section 42 in Kota Tinggi, a coastal erosion control project in Mukim Rimba Terjun in Pontian, and a similar project in Pantai Seri Menanti, Muar.

“Also carried out were the preliminary works for the People’s Residency Programme Batu Pahat and the preliminary design work for constructing a shortcut from Bakri (FT024) to Bukit Pasir (J32) in Muar,” he said today.

He said this while presenting the Johor Budget 2027 at the Johor State Assembly (DUN) session at the Sultan Ismail Building, Kota Iskandar here.

According to him, preliminary work on the conservation project for the estuary of Sungai Sedili Besar, Kota Tinggi, and the estuary of Sungai Sekakap in Mersing was also carried out.

In addition, he said another project involves preliminary work to build medians, U-turns and related work on the Batu Pahat-Ayer Hitam-Kluang Road (FT050) from Ayer Hitam to Kluang and then Batu Pahat up to the Kluang Stadium intersection.

“Upgrading of Yong Peng Road (FT24) from the Yong Peng Utara Toll Plaza to the Parit Yaani Intersection (J125) will also be carried out,” he said.

Onn Hafiz said the projects in Johor Bahru and Iskandar Puteri include upgrading 21 units of elevators at Sultan Ismail Hospital, preliminary work on the construction of the Second Permas Jaya Bridge and an elevated interchange on the Eastern Dispersal Link (EDL) Expressway.

In addition, he said that the construction of a new elevated interchange on the Second Link Malaysia-Singapore Motorway at kilometre 18 and the improvement of the Gelang Patah (J4) road network towards the Sultan Ibrahim Stadium are also being carried out.

Earlier, Onn Hafiz tabled the Johor Budget 2027 with an allocation of RM3.06 billion and a projected surplus of RM2.33 million. — Bernama
